title: Defending Infrastructure
objective: Can place the minimum necessary defensive boundaries at each layer: the internet perimeter, workloads, and VPCs.

sections.title: Restrict public entry points to the required paths
paragraphs: For public applications, separate the responsibilities of DNS, the CDN, AWS WAF, the load balancer, and the application. Accept only the required protocols and hosts, and verify together where TLS terminates, which certificates are used, how rate limiting is applied, which application-layer rules are enforced, and whether the origin is reachable.

By making CloudFront the only public viewer entry point and using an internal ALB in private subnets as a VPC origin, you can deliver content without creating a path that reaches the ALB directly through a public IP address. Simply adding WAF rules does not prevent bypass if another public path exists. A Web ACL is not an independent hop placed in the middle of the network path; it is a boundary associated with CloudFront or the ALB that evaluates requests. Observe the path from the entry point to the origin, the logs, and the effects of the rules, and evaluate the impact on legitimate users.

sections.title: Manage execution permissions and updates for each workload
paragraphs: For computing workloads, manage execution roles, the provenance of images or packages, vulnerability management, secrets, OS or runtime updates, and log delivery. Do not place shared administrator credentials in the workload; ensure that it can access only the AWS APIs and data it needs.

Perform updates as an operational process that includes validation, phased deployment, health checks, and rollback. If you stop monitoring or backups to rush patching, investigating the cause of an incident and recovering from it become more difficult.

sections.title: Verify Communication Paths and Permission Boundaries Separately
paragraphs: VPC reachability is determined by the combination of route tables, security groups, network ACLs, and host or service settings. Having a route does not mean that a port is permitted, so verify both the outbound path and the return path.

In a defensive design, separate public, private, and isolated subnets according to their purposes, and allow only the required paths and protocols. Instead of resolving connectivity problems by opening everything, use flow logs and connection logs to identify the boundary at which the traffic was denied.

checkpoints.prompt: The team responsible for a public web application wants users to access it only through CloudFront. Which design is most appropriate for closing paths that could connect to the origin without passing AWS WAF inspection?

choices.text: Use an internal-facing ALB in a private subnet as CloudFront's VPC origin, and associate a Web ACL with CloudFront or the ALB. Do not create a public path that allows direct access to the ALB from anywhere other than CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Limiting the viewer's public entry point to CloudFront and using an internal-facing ALB ensures that there is no path to a public ALB without AWS WAF evaluation.

choices.text: Expose the origin so that anyone can connect to it directly.
choices.explanation: This allows the entry-point security boundary to be bypassed.

choices.text: Configure only WAF rules and do not verify reachability to the origin.
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent direct access through other paths.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for a containerized business application wants to minimize the workload’s AWS API permissions. Which policy is most appropriate?

choices.text: Do not verify the image’s provenance or vulnerabilities in order to make updates easier.
choices.explanation: Supply chain and operational risks remain.

choices.text: Grant only the permissions for the APIs and resources required to a workload-dedicated execution role, and do not place shared administrator credentials in the workload.
choices.explanation: This limits both the execution principal and the scope of its permissions.

choices.text: Embed the same administrator access key in every container.
choices.explanation: The impact of a leak would be significant, and the principal could not be identified.

checkpoints.prompt: Investigate the issue preventing access to a service in a private subnet. Which check is most appropriate?

choices.text: Check the outbound and return routes, the destination security group, the subnet NACL, and the service configuration in sequence.
choices.explanation: This isolates routing and permissions as separate boundaries.

choices.text: Allow unrestricted access on all ports.
choices.explanation: This removes the security boundary without identifying the cause.

choices.text: Check only the route on the source side.
choices.explanation: This overlooks the return path and rejections on the destination side.
